name: Generic rooted Android phone (fallback)

charge_control.note: Qualcomm kernels: suspends USB input, so the phone runs from the battery while charging is stopped. USB data (tethering) stays up.
Older Qualcomm kernels: stops charging while USB keeps powering the phone. On some kernels it exists but has no effect: verify.
Older Qualcomm kernels: same as charging_enabled. Verify.
Samsung (models without their own profile): stops charging; on most kernels it also cuts USB input power.
OPLUS kernels (OnePlus 9 and later, Oppo, Realme). Uncertain: verify.
MediaTek: bypass (idle) mode on some kernels. Uncertain: verify.
MediaTek: the value contains a space (the ACC project writes it as 0::1). Uncertain: verify.
Linux standard end threshold, rare on Android: a value below the current charge stops charging. Uncertain: verify.

autoboot.note: Prove automatic power-on in Phase 0 (plan 4.3): phones with fastboot try 'fastboot oem off-mode-charge 0'; others need a root change that makes the charging-only mode boot Android. Check with tools/phase0/phase0.sh autoboot --test.

notes: Fallback used when no other profile matches this phone. Write a device profile for any phone that goes outdoors (docs/device-profiles.md).

Charge-control candidates are tried in order and the first existing, writable path wins, so an ineffective file earlier in the list can hide a working one. Prove the path with tools/phase0/phase0.sh charge-discover --test and put it first in a device profile.

current_now assumes microamps, positive while charging (Android's BatteryManager convention). Many Qualcomm kernels report the opposite sign and some report milliamps: measure with tools/phase0/phase0.sh current-sign.
Thermal keywords leave out Qualcomm battery-current-limit zones such as 'soc', 'vbat' and 'ibat': they report charge level, voltage or current, not temperature.
